findings: Broken cross-reference: change control procedure is said to be in Section 9, but the Agreement has no Section 9 (it ends at Section 8). 2.4
Arithmetic error: annual Fee of $58,000 is said to represent twelve monthly payments, but 12 × $4,750 = $57,000. 3.3 (with 3.2)
Direct contradiction: Section 3.5 gives 45-day terms for invoices over $10,000, while Section 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices without exception. 3.5 / 3.6
Internal tension: monthly Fee is 'payable in advance' yet invoices are payable 30 days after invoice date, leaving the actual due date undetermined. 3.2 / 3.4
Fee inconsistency with Appendix A: Section 3.2 states a monthly Fee of $4,750 but Appendix A's itemized total is $4,690 (a $60 discrepancy). 3.2 / Appendix A
Undefined term: 'Restricted Data' is used but never defined (the Agreement only defines 'Personal Data'). 4.2
Undefined term: 'Territory' is used in the definition of Business Day and in the data transfer restriction but is never defined. 1.5 / 4.2
Undefined role: 'Data Steward' is referenced as the party holding record-keeping obligations but is never defined or appointed anywhere. 4.4
Direct contradiction in breach notification deadline: 72 hours (Section 4.5) versus three Business Days (Section 4.7), which can be substantially longer given weekends and holidays. 4.5 / 4.7

Reference to a document outside the Agreement: Appendix C is cited as containing the security measures, but Section 1.1 defines the Agreement as including only Appendices A and B, and no Appendix C is attached. 4.6 / 1.1
Defined term 'Permitted Subprocessor' is never used; Section 4.8 addresses subprocessors without invoking the definition, leaving the definition orphaned. 1.7 / 4.8
Circular definition: 'Confidential Information' is defined as 'information that is confidential', providing no operative criterion. 1.3

Definitional gap: 'Security Incident' covers only unauthorized access or disclosure, omitting accidental loss, alteration or destruction of Personal Data, so such events trigger no notification duty. 1.6
Undefined term: 'Business Hours' is used for the Priority 1 response commitment but is never defined (only 'Business Day' is defined). 5.2
Inconsistent service commitment: Section 5.2 promises response within four Business Hours while Appendix A item A-3 promises a '4 hour response'. 5.2 / Appendix A A-3
Arithmetic error: 99.5% monthly availability permits approximately 3.6 hours of downtime in a 30-day month (0.5% of 720 hours), not the stated three (3) hours. 5.3
Contradiction: service credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee are promised in Section 5.4 but capped at 10% of the monthly Fee in Section 5.5, making the 25% tier unattainable. 5.4 / 5.5
Logical gap in credit tiers: overlapping thresholds (below 99.5%, below 99%, below 95%) do not state whether credits are cumulative or exclusive. 5.4

Conflict with liability carve-outs: service credits are stated as the sole remedy for service level failures, which conflicts with the uncapped/unrestricted liability preserved in Section 7.3. 5.6 / 7.3

Circular / broken definition of Effective Date: commencement is tied to the Effective Date 'as defined in the prior Master Services Agreement', yet Section 8.1 supersedes that prior agreement and fixes a different commencement date (1 January 2027). 'Effective Date' is also absent from Section 1. 6.1 / 8.1
Contradiction: Section 6.4 permits immediate termination for uncured material breach, but Section 6.5 states the 60-day notice period may not be shortened or waived by either party. 6.4 / 6.5
Gap: automatic renewal is stated to occur 'unless terminated' with no non-renewal notice deadline specified relative to the renewal date. 6.2
Survival inconsistency: Section 6.6 lists only Sections 1, 4 and 8 as surviving, while Section 7.5 states Section 7 also survives. 6.6 / 7.5
Contradiction: Section 7.4 states the liability cap applies notwithstanding any other provision, which negates the express carve-out in Section 7.3. 7.3 / 7.4

Asymmetric/unworkable cap: the mutual liability cap is measured solely by Fees paid by Customer, giving no coherent measure for Customer's own liability and leaving the cap at $0 before any payment. 7.2
Governing law contradiction: Section 8.3 selects Washington law while Section 8.4 requires Delaware courts to apply Delaware law. 8.3 / 8.4
Conflict between unilateral modification right (Section 2.2) and the requirement that any change to scope be agreed in writing under change control (Section 2.4). 2.2 / 2.4
Appendix A lists a 'Quarterly analytics review' with a monthly charge of $640, conflating quarterly delivery with monthly billing without reconciliation. Appendix A A-4
Appendix A includes item A-5 marked 'Reserved' with no description or charge, leaving an undefined line item in the service catalog. Appendix A A-5
Interest rate of 1.5% per month (18% p.a.) is stated without any cap for the maximum permitted by applicable law, and applies even to invoices whose due date is indeterminate under 3.4/3.5/3.6. 3.7

findings: Circular/self-referential definition: "Confidential Information" is defined as "information that is confidential," providing no substantive test for what qualifies. 1.3
"Territory" is used but never defined anywhere in the Agreement (also relied on in 4.2). 1.5
"Permitted Subprocessor" is defined but never used in the operative text; Section 4.8 refers only to "subprocessors," leaving the definition orphaned. 1.7

Circular definition: "Fees" means amounts payable under Section 3, while Section 3.1 says Customer shall pay "the Fees" in accordance with Section 3 — neither provision independently fixes the obligation. 1.8 / 3.1

"Agreement" is defined as this document plus Appendix A and Appendix B only, yet Section 4.6 incorporates Appendix C; Appendix C is therefore outside the Agreement and is also not attached to the document. 1.1 / 4.6
Broken cross-reference: the change control procedure is said to be "set out in Section 9," but the Agreement contains only Sections 1–8. 2.4
Arithmetic error: twelve monthly payments of $4,750 equal $57,000, not the stated annual prepayment figure of $58,000. 3.2 / 3.3
Direct contradiction on payment terms: 3.4 sets 30 days, 3.5 sets 45 days for invoices over $10,000, and 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception." 3.4 / 3.5 / 3.6
Contradictory Security Incident notification deadlines: 72 hours in 4.5 versus three Business Days in 4.7 (which, over a weekend or holiday, is materially longer). 4.5 / 4.7
"Restricted Data" is an undefined term; the Agreement only defines "Personal Data" and "Confidential Information," so the transfer restriction has no ascertainable subject matter. 4.2
"Data Steward" is an undefined term; no party, role, or appointment mechanism is established, so the record-keeping obligation has no identified obligor. 4.4
"Business Hours" is used for the Priority 1 response commitment but is never defined (only "Business Day" is defined). 5.2
Arithmetic error: 0.5% unavailability of a month (~720–744 hours) is approximately 3.6–3.7 hours, not the stated maximum of three (3) hours; the percentage and hour figures are inconsistent. 5.3
Service credit tiers conflict with the aggregate cap: credits of 25% (below 95%) and 10% (below 99%) cannot be paid under the 10% monthly cap, making the 25% tier inoperative. 5.4 / 5.5
Overlapping, non-exclusive credit tiers: availability below 95% is also below 99% and below 99.5%, and the document does not state whether tiers are cumulative or mutually exclusive. 5.4

Logical gap: 5.1 imposes only a "commercially reasonable efforts" standard, while 5.4 creates automatic credit entitlement on any shortfall, leaving it unclear whether failure despite reasonable efforts triggers credits. 5.1 / 5.4

Circular/broken definition of the Effective Date: 6.1 defines it by reference to the prior Master Services Agreement, while 8.1 states this Agreement supersedes that prior agreement and takes effect 1 January 2027 — the reference source is extinguished and the two commencement dates conflict. 6.1 / 8.1
Contradiction: 6.5 states the 60-day notice period may not be shortened or waived, yet 6.4 permits immediate termination for uncured material breach. 6.4 / 6.5
Survival clause conflict: 6.6 lists only Sections 1, 4 and 8 as surviving, while 7.5 states Section 7 survives termination. 6.6 / 7.5
Contradiction: 7.4 states the liability cap applies "notwithstanding any other provision," which negates the express carve-out in 7.3 for Security Incidents caused by Provider's negligence. 7.3 / 7.4
The liability cap is measured solely by "Fees paid by Customer," which is incoherent as a limit on Customer's own liability and undefined for claims arising in the first twelve months. 7.2
Governing law contradiction: 8.3 selects Washington law while 8.4 requires Delaware courts to apply Delaware law. 8.3 / 8.4
Appendix A total monthly charge of $4,690 (1,900+1,250+900+640) contradicts the $4,750 monthly Fee stated in Section 3.2 — a $60 discrepancy. Appendix A / 3.2
Inconsistent support commitment: Appendix A item A-3 promises a "4 hour response" whereas Section 5.2 promises four Business Hours. Appendix A (A-3) / 5.2
Item A-4 is a quarterly deliverable billed as a flat monthly charge, with no reconciliation of quarterly delivery to monthly invoicing. Appendix A (A-4)

Logical gap in renewal: automatic renewal applies "unless terminated" but no non-renewal notice deadline is specified, and it is unclear how the 60-day notice in 6.3 interacts with the renewal date. 6.2 / 6.3
"Service credits are Customer's sole remedy" conflicts with Customer's right to terminate for material breach and with the uncapped Security Incident liability route. 5.6 / 6.4 / 7.3
Provider's unilateral right to modify performance conflicts with the requirement that any change to Services scope go through written change control. 2.2 / 2.4
Definition of "Security Incident" covers only unauthorized access or disclosure, omitting accidental loss, alteration or destruction, so 4.5/4.7 notification duties do not cover such events. 1.6
Section 3.5's $10,000 threshold is effectively unreachable under monthly billing of $4,750, indicating the tier was drafted for a fee structure inconsistent with Section 3.2. 3.5

findings: Circular definition: "Confidential Information" is defined as "information that is confidential", which defines the term by itself and provides no operative test. 1.3
Undefined term "Territory" is used in the definition of Business Day (and again in 4.2) but is never defined anywhere in the Agreement or Appendices. 1.5
"Permitted Subprocessor" is defined but never used in the operative text; Section 4.8 restates the consent requirement without using the defined term. 1.7 / 4.8

Near-circular definition chain: "Fees" means amounts payable under Section 3, and Section 3.1 says Customer shall pay "the Fees" in accordance with Section 3, giving no independent substance. 1.8 / 3.1
Definition of Agreement includes only Appendix A and Appendix B, yet Section 4.6 incorporates an Appendix C; Appendix C is neither part of the Agreement nor attached. 1.1 / 4.6
Broken cross-reference: change control procedure is said to be "set out in Section 9", but the Agreement has no Section 9 (it ends at Section 8). 2.4
Potential conflict: Provider's unilateral right to modify performance is inconsistent with the requirement that any change to scope be agreed in writing under change control. 2.2 vs 2.4
Arithmetic error: twelve monthly payments of $4,750 equals $57,000, not the stated $58,000 annual Fee "representing twelve monthly payments". 3.2 / 3.3
Monthly Fee stated as $4,750 contradicts the Appendix A service catalog total monthly charge of $4,690. 3.2 vs Appendix A
Direct contradiction: 3.5 gives 45-day terms for invoices over $10,000, while 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception". 3.4–3.6
Undefined term "Restricted Data" — only "Personal Data" is defined, so the transfer restriction has no identifiable subject matter. 4.2
Undefined term/role "Data Steward" — no party, appointee, or definition establishes who this is or that Provider must appoint one. 4.4
Contradictory notification deadlines for the same event: 72 hours in 4.5 versus three (3) Business Days in 4.7 (which can be up to five or more calendar days). 4.5 vs 4.7
Undefined term "Business Hours" — the Agreement defines "Business Day" only, leaving the Priority 1 response metric unmeasurable. 5.2
Inconsistent with Appendix A item A-3, which promises a plain "4 hour response" rather than four Business Hours. 5.2 vs Appendix A
Arithmetic error: 99.5% monthly availability permits approximately 3.6 hours of downtime in a 30-day month (720 h × 0.5%), not the stated three (3) hours. 5.3
Service credit tiers are cumulative/overlapping and ambiguous: availability below 99% or 95% is also below 99.5%, so multiple tiers trigger simultaneously with no stated rule. 5.4
Contradiction: the 25% and (partly) 10% credit tiers can never be paid because 5.5 caps aggregate monthly credits at 10% of the monthly Fee, rendering the top tier inoperative. 5.4 vs 5.5
Logical gap/conflict: service credits as "sole remedy" is inconsistent with the termination right for material breach in 6.4 and with the liability carve-out in 7.3. 5.6 vs 6.4 / 7.3

Circular/contradictory Effective Date: the Effective Date is defined by reference to the prior Master Services Agreement, which 8.1 states is superseded, while 8.1 separately fixes effectiveness at 1 January 2027. 6.1 vs 8.1
Logical gap: automatic renewal "unless terminated" specifies no non-renewal notice mechanism or deadline for preventing renewal. 6.2

Conflict: immediate termination for uncured material breach cannot be reconciled with the rule that the 60-day notice period may not be shortened or waived, and prohibiting waiver of one's own notice right is internally illogical. 6.3–6.5

Direct contradiction: 7.4 states the cap applies "notwithstanding any other provision", which negates the express carve-out in 7.3 for Security Incidents caused by Provider negligence. 7.3 vs 7.4

Liability cap measured by "total Fees paid by Customer" is applied to "each party", producing an asymmetric/illogical cap on Customer's own payment liability and an undefined cap before any Fees are paid. 7.2

findings: Circular definition: "Confidential Information" is defined as "information that is confidential", defining the term by itself and providing no operative test. 1.3
Undefined term "Territory" is used to define Business Day (and again in 4.2) but is never defined anywhere in the Agreement or Appendices. 1.5 (and 4.2)

"Security Incident" is limited to unauthorized access or disclosure and omits accidental loss, alteration or destruction of Personal Data, leaving a substantive gap in the notification obligation in 4.5. 1.6
"Permitted Subprocessor" is defined but never used anywhere in the Agreement; 4.8 addresses subprocessors without using the defined term. 1.7 (cf. 4.8)

Circular cross-reference: "Fees" means amounts payable under Section 3, while 3.1 says Customer shall pay "the Fees" in accordance with Section 3 — neither provision independently fixes the amount. 1.8 / 3.1
Broken cross-reference: the change control procedure is said to be "set out in Section 9", but the Agreement has no Section 9 (it ends at Section 8). 2.4
Contradiction: 2.2 permits Provider to unilaterally modify performance, while 2.4 requires any change to the Services to be agreed in writing under change control. 2.2 vs 2.4
Arithmetic error: twelve monthly payments of $4,750 equal $57,000, not the stated annual Fee of $58,000. 3.3 (with 3.2)
Direct contradiction: 3.5 gives 45-day terms for invoices over $10,000, but 3.6 states the 30-day term in 3.4 applies to all invoices "without exception". 3.5 vs 3.6 (and 3.4)
Fee inconsistency: the stated monthly Fee of $4,750 does not match the Appendix A service catalog total of $4,690 (difference of $60). 3.2 vs Appendix A
Undefined term "Restricted Data" — the Agreement defines Personal Data and Confidential Information but never Restricted Data, so the transfer restriction has no identifiable subject matter. 4.2
Undefined term/role "Data Steward" — no party, appointment mechanism, or definition is provided, so the record-keeping obligation is unattributable. 4.4
Direct contradiction in notification deadlines: 4.5 requires notice within 72 hours while 4.7 allows three Business Days (which may exceed 72 hours over a weekend or holiday). 4.5 vs 4.7
Reference to Appendix C, which does not exist and is excluded from the definition of "Agreement" in 1.1 (only Appendices A and B). 4.6 (with 1.1)
Redundant/overlapping obligation: 4.8 restates the subprocessor consent requirement already embedded in the definition of Permitted Subprocessor, with no reconciliation. 4.8 vs 1.7
Inconsistent standard of obligation: 5.1 imposes only "commercially reasonable efforts" for the service levels, while 5.3 imposes an absolute obligation to "maintain" 99.5% availability. 5.1 vs 5.3
Undefined term "Business Hours" (only "Business Day" is defined), leaving the Priority 1 response time unmeasurable. 5.2
Arithmetic error: 99.5% availability measured monthly permits approximately 3.6 hours of downtime in a 30-day month (720 × 0.5%), not the stated three (3) hours. 5.3

Overlapping, non-exclusive credit tiers: availability below 95% is simultaneously below 99% and below 99.5%, so 5% / 10% / 25% credits can all be triggered by one event with no rule of precedence. 5.4
Contradiction: 5.4 provides a 25% service credit (and cumulative tiers) while 5.5 caps aggregate monthly credits at 10% of the monthly Fee, making the 25% tier unachievable. 5.4 vs 5.5

Ambiguous trigger: 5.4 applies where availability is "below 99.5%" and 5.3 requires "at least 99.5%", but 5.4's opening words refer to falling "below the levels stated" without identifying which level. 5.3 / 5.4

Conflict with liability regime: 5.6 makes service credits the sole remedy for service level failures, yet 7.3 removes the liability cap for Security Incidents and 7.4 says the cap applies notwithstanding any other provision. 5.6 vs 7.3/7.4

Circular/broken definition of Effective Date: it is defined by reference to the prior Master Services Agreement, which 8.1 expressly supersedes; the preamble also uses "Effective Date" as if defined in Section 1, where it is not. 6.1 (with 8.1 and preamble)
Date contradiction: 8.1 fixes commencement at 1 January 2027 while 6.1 ties commencement to the Effective Date under the superseded prior agreement. 6.1 vs 8.1
Contradiction: 6.3 allows either party to terminate at will on 60 days' notice, which nullifies the 24-month initial term (6.1) and the automatic renewal structure (6.2). 6.1/6.2 vs 6.3
Gap: automatic renewal "unless terminated" specifies no non-renewal notice deadline or mechanism. 6.2
Contradiction: 6.4 permits immediate termination for uncured material breach, but 6.5 states the 60-day notice period may not be shortened or waived by either party. 6.4 vs 6.5
Inconsistent survival clauses: 6.6 lists only Sections 1, 4 and 8 as surviving, while 7.5 states Section 7 survives; accrued payment obligations under Section 3 are also omitted. 6.6 vs 7.5
Internal contradiction: 7.4 says the cap applies notwithstanding any other provision, which negates the express carve-out in 7.3 for Security Incidents caused by Provider's negligence. 7.3 vs 7.4

Logical gap: the cap is measured by "Fees paid by Customer", giving Customer an unlimited-in-practice benefit and Provider a meaningless cap in the first year; it is also unworkable as a cap on Customer's own liability for unpaid Fees. 7.2
Unreconciled overlap: 7.6 excludes indirect and consequential loss absolutely, without carving out the Security Incident liability preserved by 7.3. 7.6 vs 7.3
Governing law contradiction: 8.3 selects Washington law while 8.4 requires Delaware courts to apply Delaware law. 8.3 vs 8.4

Appendix A includes item A-5 "Reserved" with no description or charge, and A-4 is a quarterly service billed as a monthly charge, creating inconsistency with the definition of Services in 1.2. Appendix A (with 1.2)
Appendix A item A-3 states a "4 hour response" while 5.2 requires response within four Business Hours — different measurement units for the same commitment. Appendix A A-3 vs 5.2
unmatched: "Security Incident" is limited to unauthorized access or disclosure and omits accidental loss, alteration or destruction of Personal Data, leaving a substantive gap in the notification obligation in 4.5. 1.6

Circular cross-reference: "Fees" means amounts payable under Section 3, while 3.1 says Customer shall pay "the Fees" in accordance with Section 3 — neither provision independently fixes the amount. 1.8 / 3.1
Contradiction: 2.2 permits Provider to unilaterally modify performance, while 2.4 requires any change to the Services to be agreed in writing under change control. 2.2 vs 2.4
Undefined term "Business Hours" (only "Business Day" is defined), leaving the Priority 1 response time unmeasurable. 5.2
Contradiction: 6.3 allows either party to terminate at will on 60 days' notice, which nullifies the 24-month initial term (6.1) and the automatic renewal structure (6.2). 6.1/6.2 vs 6.3
Gap: automatic renewal "unless terminated" specifies no non-renewal notice deadline or mechanism. 6.2

Logical gap: the cap is measured by "Fees paid by Customer", giving Customer an unlimited-in-practice benefit and Provider a meaningless cap in the first year; it is also unworkable as a cap on Customer's own liability for unpaid Fees. 7.2

findings: Circular definition: "Confidential Information" is defined as "information that is confidential", which defines the term by reference to itself and provides no operative test. 1.3
Undefined term: "Territory" is used in the definition of Business Day (and again in 4.2) but is never defined anywhere in the Agreement or Appendices. 1.5

Defined term "Permitted Subprocessor" is never used in the body of the Agreement; Section 4.8 addresses subprocessors without using or referencing the definition, making it orphaned/redundant. 1.7 / 4.8

Broken cross-reference: the Agreement is defined as comprising only Appendix A and Appendix B, yet Section 4.6 incorporates an Appendix C that is neither part of the Agreement nor attached. 1.1 (with 4.6)
Broken cross-reference: change control procedure is said to be "set out in Section 9", but the Agreement ends at Section 8; there is no Section 9. 2.4

Logical tension: Provider may unilaterally modify performance under 2.2 while 2.4 requires all scope changes to be agreed in writing; no rule resolves which governs a modification that alters scope without reducing functionality. 2.2 / 2.4
Arithmetic error: the stated annual Fee of $58,000 does not equal twelve monthly payments of $4,750, which is $57,000 (a $1,000 discrepancy). 3.3 (with 3.2)
Direct contradiction: 3.5 gives a 45-day payment term for invoices over $10,000, while 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception". 3.5 / 3.6
Inconsistency with Appendix A: the monthly Fee is stated as $4,750, but the Appendix A service catalog totals $4,690 (a $60 discrepancy). 3.2 (with Appendix A)
Undefined term: "Restricted Data" appears only here; the Agreement defines "Personal Data" and "Confidential Information" but never "Restricted Data". 4.2
Undefined term/role: "Data Steward" is referenced as bearing an obligation but is never defined, appointed, or attributed to either party. 4.4

Direct contradiction: 4.5 requires Security Incident notification within 72 hours, while 4.7 requires notification within three Business Days (which can exceed 72 hours over weekends/holidays); no precedence rule is given. 4.5 / 4.7

Contradiction: 5.4 provides a 25% service credit for availability below 95%, but 5.5 caps aggregate monthly credits at 10% of the monthly Fee, making the 25% tier unattainable. 5.4 / 5.5

Logical gap: the service credit tiers overlap (availability below 95% is also below 99% and 99.5%) with no rule stating that only the highest applicable tier applies or whether credits are cumulative. 5.4

Logical gap: 5.1 commits only to "commercially reasonable efforts" to meet service levels, but 5.4 triggers credits on any failure to meet them, leaving unclear whether a breach is required. 5.1 / 5.4

Contradiction: 6.6 lists only Sections 1, 4 and 8 as surviving termination, while 7.5 states Section 7 also survives; Section 7 is omitted from the survival list. 6.6 / 7.5
Contradiction: 7.3 carves Security Incidents caused by Provider negligence out of the liability cap, while 7.4 states the cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of the Agreement. 7.3 / 7.4

Contradiction: 5.6 makes service credits the sole remedy for service level failures, while Section 7 preserves uncapped liability for negligence-caused Security Incidents that may also constitute service level failures; no reconciliation is provided. 5.6 / 7.3
Governing law conflict: 8.3 selects Washington law while 8.4 requires Delaware courts to apply Delaware law to any dispute. 8.3 / 8.4

Liability cap is indeterminate in early stages: it is measured by Fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, with no floor or method for claims arising before twelve months of Fees have been paid. 7.2

findings: Broken cross-reference: refers to a change control procedure in "Section 9", but the Agreement has no Section 9 (it ends at Section 8). 2.4

Appendix C is referenced for the technical and organizational measures, but Section 1.1 defines the Agreement as comprising only Appendix A and Appendix B, and no Appendix C is attached. 4.6 (with 1.1)
Circular/vacuous definition: "Confidential Information" is defined as "information that is confidential", providing no operative criteria. 1.3
Circular definition pair: "Fees" means amounts payable under Section 3, while Section 3.1 states Customer shall pay "the Fees" in accordance with Section 3. 1.8 and 3.1
Undefined term "Territory" is used in the definition of Business Day (and again in 4.2) but is never defined. 1.5 (and 4.2)
Defined term "Permitted Subprocessor" is never used anywhere in the Agreement; Section 4.8 instead restates a consent requirement without using the defined term. 1.7 / 4.8
Undefined term "Restricted Data" — the data protection provisions otherwise operate on "Personal Data"; no definition of Restricted Data exists. 4.2
Undefined term/role "Data Steward" — no party or person is identified as the Data Steward, so the record-keeping obligation has no identified obligor. 4.4
Undefined term "Business Hours" — only "Business Day" is defined, leaving the Priority 1 response deadline indeterminate. 5.2

Arithmetic/internal contradiction: annual prepayment of $58,000 is said to represent twelve monthly payments, but 12 × $4,750 = $57,000 (a $1,000 discrepancy), and a prepayment priced above the monthly aggregate is illogical. 3.2–3.3
Direct contradiction: Section 3.5 imposes a 45-day term for invoices over $10,000 while Section 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception". 3.4–3.6
Fee inconsistency: the monthly Fee is stated as $4,750, but the Appendix A service catalog totals $4,690 for the same Services. 3.2 vs Appendix A
Contradictory notification deadlines for a Security Incident: 72 hours in 4.5 versus three (3) Business Days in 4.7 (which can be considerably longer given weekends/holidays). 4.5 vs 4.7
Availability arithmetic error: 99.5% monthly availability permits roughly 3.6 hours of downtime in a 30-day month (0.5% of ~720 hours), not "no more than three (3) hours". 5.3
Service credit cap contradicts the credit table: the 25% (below 95%) and arguably the 10% tiers can never be paid because aggregate monthly credits are capped at 10% of the monthly Fee. 5.4 vs 5.5
Overlapping, non-exclusive credit tiers: availability below 99% or below 95% is also "below 99.5%", and the clause does not state that only the highest applicable tier applies. 5.4
Logical tension: Provider owes only "commercially reasonable efforts" to meet service levels, yet 5.4 imposes automatic credits for any shortfall regardless of effort. 5.1 vs 5.4

Circular/contradictory Effective Date: the Effective Date is defined by reference to the prior Master Services Agreement, which Section 8.1 says this Agreement supersedes, while also fixing effectiveness at 1 January 2027. 6.1 vs 8.1

Contradiction: Section 6.5 states the 60-day notice period may not be shortened or waived, which conflicts with the immediate termination right for material breach in 6.4 and with the parties' general freedom to agree otherwise. 6.4–6.5

Logical gap in the breach termination mechanism: no requirement to give notice of breach or to specify when the 15-day cure period begins, yet termination is available "immediately" once the breach remains uncured. 6.4
Survival inconsistency: Section 6.6 lists only Sections 1, 4 and 8 as surviving, while Section 7.5 states Section 7 survives termination. 6.6 vs 7.5
Auto-renewal gap: renewal occurs "unless terminated" with no stated non-renewal notice deadline, and the 60-day notice right in 6.3 is not tied to renewal dates. 6.2
Contradiction: 7.3 creates an exception to the liability cap for negligence-caused Security Incidents, but 7.4 states the cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of the Agreement. 7.3 vs 7.4
Governing law versus forum contradiction: the Agreement is governed by Washington law, yet 8.4 requires Delaware courts to apply Delaware law. 8.3 vs 8.4

Sole-remedy clause conflicts with the liability regime: 5.6 makes service credits the sole remedy for service level failures even where the failure involves a negligent Security Incident carved out of the cap by 7.3. 5.6 vs 7.3
Response time inconsistency: Appendix A item A-3 promises a "4 hour response", while Section 5.2 promises four Business Hours. Appendix A (A-3) vs 5.2
Unilateral modification right in 2.2 conflicts with the requirement in 2.4 that any change to scope be agreed in writing via change control. 2.2 vs 2.4

Liability cap is unworkable as applied to Customer: capping "each party's" liability at Fees paid would cap Customer's own payment obligations, and no Fees will have been paid for claims arising in the first months. 7.2
Appendix A includes a line item "A-5 Reserved" with no charge or description, leaving an undefined placeholder in the contractual service catalog. Appendix A (A-5)
Seat limit "up to 40 seats" in Appendix A has no corresponding provision on excess-seat pricing or consequences of exceeding it. Appendix A (A-2)
Definition of Security Incident covers only unauthorized access or disclosure, omitting loss, destruction or alteration of Personal Data, leaving those events without a notification obligation. 1.6

findings: Circular definition: "Confidential Information" is defined as "information that is confidential", which defines the term by itself and provides no operative criteria. 1.3
Undefined term "Territory" is used in the definition of Business Day (and again in 4.2) but is never defined anywhere in the Agreement or Appendices. 1.5 (and 4.2)
"Permitted Subprocessor" is defined but never used in the body of the Agreement; Section 4.8 addresses subprocessors without reference to the defined term. 1.7 / 4.8
Broken cross-reference: the change control procedure is said to be set out in Section 9, but the Agreement has no Section 9 (it ends at Section 8). 2.4
Arithmetic error/internal contradiction: $4,750 × 12 = $57,000, not $58,000, so the annual Fee cannot represent twelve monthly payments. 3.3 (with 3.2)

Contradiction between payment terms: 3.4 sets 30 days, 3.5 sets 45 days for invoices over $10,000, and 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception", making 3.5 inoperable. 3.4–3.6
The monthly Fee stated in the body ($4,750) contradicts the total monthly charge in the Service Catalog ($4,690). 3.2 vs Appendix A
Undefined term "Restricted Data"; the data protection section otherwise regulates "Personal Data", so the transfer restriction has no defined subject matter. 4.2
Undefined role "Data Steward" — no party, appointee, or definition establishes who this is or which party bears the record-keeping obligation. 4.4
Contradictory notification deadlines for a Security Incident: 72 hours (4.5) versus three Business Days (4.7), which can differ by several days over a weekend/holiday. 4.5 vs 4.7

Reference to Appendix C, which does not exist and is excluded from the definition of "Agreement" (which lists only Appendices A and B); the technical and organizational measures are therefore undefined. 4.6 (with 1.1)

Definition of "Security Incident" covers only unauthorized access or disclosure, omitting loss, alteration or destruction of Personal Data, leaving a gap in the notification obligation and in the liability carve-out at 7.3. 1.6
Undefined term "Business Hours" (only "Business Day" is defined), so the Priority 1 response commitment is unmeasurable. 5.2
Undefined term "Priority 1" — no severity classification or triage criteria are established anywhere. 5.2 / Appendix A item A-3
Inconsistency between the Service Catalog's "4 hour response" for Priority 1 support and the Agreement's "four (4) Business Hours" commitment. Appendix A item A-3 vs 5.2
Arithmetic error: 99.5% monthly availability permits approximately 3.6 hours of downtime in a 30-day month (0.5% of 720 hours), not three (3) hours; the stated figures are inconsistent. 5.3
Contradiction: the service credit schedule provides credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, but 5.5 caps aggregate monthly credits at 10%, rendering the 25% tier unattainable. 5.4 vs 5.5
Logical gap: the credit tiers overlap (availability below 95% is also below 99% and 99.5%) with no rule stating whether credits are cumulative or whether only the highest tier applies. 5.4

Circular/contradictory commencement provision: the Effective Date is defined by reference to the prior Master Services Agreement, which 8.1 states is superseded, and 8.1 separately fixes effect on 1 January 2027. 6.1 vs 8.1
Contradiction: 6.4 permits immediate termination on written notice for uncured material breach, while 6.5 states the 60-day notice period may not be shortened or waived by either party. 6.4 vs 6.5

Contradiction: 6.3 allows termination on 60 days' notice at any time, which is irreconcilable with an automatic renewal regime in 6.2 that specifies no non-renewal notice mechanism; 6.2 also fails to state how renewal is prevented. 6.2 vs 6.3
Survival clause omits Section 7 while 7.5 states Section 7 survives termination — inconsistent survival lists; Section 5 credits and Section 3 payment obligations are also unaddressed. 6.6 vs 7.5
Direct contradiction: 7.3 carves Security Incident negligence claims out of the liability cap, while 7.4 states the cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of the Agreement. 7.3 vs 7.4

Logical asymmetry: capping "each party's" liability at Fees paid by Customer makes Customer's cap self-referential to its own payments and provides no meaningful cap where Customer has paid little or nothing. 7.2
Governing law/jurisdiction contradiction: 8.3 selects Washington law while 8.4 requires Delaware courts to apply Delaware law. 8.3 vs 8.4
Contradiction with the preamble, which states the Agreement takes effect on the Effective Date, whereas 8.1 fixes a specific effective date of 1 January 2027. 8.1 vs Preamble

Section 5.6 makes service credits the sole remedy for service level failures, which conflicts with the unqualified liability carve-out in 7.3 for Provider-caused Security Incidents affecting availability, and no priority rule is given. 5.6 vs 7.3

Appendix A item A-5 is "Reserved" with no charge or description, and the catalog contains no provision for seats beyond the 40-seat dashboard limit or for the quarterly review being billed monthly — an internal inconsistency in charging basis. Appendix A
unmatched: Definition of "Security Incident" covers only unauthorized access or disclosure, omitting loss, alteration or destruction of Personal Data, leaving a gap in the notification obligation and in the liability carve-out at 7.3. 1.6
Undefined term "Business Hours" (only "Business Day" is defined), so the Priority 1 response commitment is unmeasurable. 5.2
Undefined term "Priority 1" — no severity classification or triage criteria are established anywhere. 5.2 / Appendix A item A-3

Contradiction: 6.3 allows termination on 60 days' notice at any time, which is irreconcilable with an automatic renewal regime in 6.2 that specifies no non-renewal notice mechanism; 6.2 also fails to state how renewal is prevented. 6.2 vs 6.3

Logical asymmetry: capping "each party's" liability at Fees paid by Customer makes Customer's cap self-referential to its own payments and provides no meaningful cap where Customer has paid little or nothing. 7.2
Contradiction with the preamble, which states the Agreement takes effect on the Effective Date, whereas 8.1 fixes a specific effective date of 1 January 2027. 8.1 vs Preamble

findings: Circular definition: "Confidential Information" is defined as "information that is confidential", which defines the term by reference to itself and provides no operative test. 1.3
Undefined term "Territory" — used to define Business Day (and again in 4.2) but never defined anywhere in the Agreement. 1.5
"Permitted Subprocessor" is defined but never used anywhere in the Agreement (orphan definition); Section 4.8 instead states the consent requirement in free-standing terms. 1.7

Arithmetic error: $4,750 monthly × 12 = $57,000, not $58,000, so the annual Fee cannot represent "twelve monthly payments". 3.3
Direct contradiction: 3.5 gives a 45-day term for invoices over $10,000 while 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception". 3.5 / 3.6

findings: Broken cross-reference: change control procedure is said to be in Section 9, but the Agreement has no Section 9 (it ends at Section 8 plus appendices). 2.4
Undefined term 'Territory' used in the definition of Business Day (and again in 4.2) but never defined anywhere. 1.5
Circular/self-referential definition: 'Confidential Information' means information 'that is confidential', which defines the term by itself and provides no operative test. 1.3
Defined term 'Permitted Subprocessor' is never used in the Agreement; Section 4.8 instead refers to 'subprocessors' without the defined approval mechanism. 1.7 / 4.8

Appendix C is referenced as containing the technical and organizational measures, but Appendix C is not attached and, per Section 1.1, the Agreement consists only of Appendices A and B — so the referenced measures do not exist within the Agreement. 4.6 (and 1.1)
Undefined term 'Restricted Data' — the data protection provisions elsewhere use 'Personal Data'; 'Restricted Data' is never defined, so the transfer restriction has no identifiable subject. 4.2
Undefined term/role 'Data Steward' — no such party or position is defined or appointed anywhere in the Agreement. 4.4
Undefined term 'Business Hours' — only 'Business Day' is defined, so the Priority 1 response obligation is unmeasurable. 5.2

Arithmetic error: twelve monthly payments of $4,750 equal $57,000, not the stated annual fee of $58,000 (a $1,000 discrepancy), and $58,000 is described as 'representing twelve monthly payments'. 3.3 (with 3.2)

Internal contradiction on payment terms: 3.4 sets 30 days, 3.5 sets 45 days for invoices over $10,000, and 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices 'without exception', directly negating 3.5. 3.4–3.6

Logical gap: with a monthly Fee of $4,750 payable in advance, no monthly invoice can exceed $10,000, making the 45-day tier inoperative except possibly for annual prepayment, which is not addressed. 3.5

Arithmetic error: 99.5% monthly availability permits approximately 3.65 hours of downtime in a 30-day month (730 hours), not 'no more than three (3) hours'; three hours corresponds to about 99.59% availability. 5.3

Contradiction between service credit tiers and the aggregate cap: credits of 25% (below 95%) and 10% (below 99%) cannot be paid because 5.5 caps aggregate monthly credits at 10% of the monthly Fee, rendering the 25% tier meaningless. 5.4 / 5.5
Overlapping/ambiguous credit tiers: availability below 95% is simultaneously 'below 99.5%', 'below 99%' and 'below 95%', and the clause does not state whether tiers are exclusive or cumulative. 5.4

Contradiction in notification deadline for Security Incidents: 4.5 requires notice within 72 hours while 4.7 requires notice within three Business Days (which can be substantially longer over weekends/holidays). 4.5 / 4.7

Circular/unworkable definition of commencement: the Effective Date is defined by reference to the prior Master Services Agreement, which Section 8.1 states is superseded by this Agreement, so the defining instrument no longer exists. 6.1 (with 8.1)
Contradiction on effective date: the preamble and 6.1 say the Agreement takes effect on the Effective Date (from the prior MSA), while 8.1 fixes commencement at 1 January 2027. 8.1 / preamble / 6.1

Contradiction on termination notice: 6.5 states the 60-day notice period may not be shortened or waived, which conflicts with 6.4's right to terminate immediately for uncured material breach (and arguably with any negotiated waiver). 6.5 / 6.4
Inconsistent survival provisions: 6.6 lists only Sections 1, 4 and 8 as surviving, while 7.5 states Section 7 survives termination; Section 7 is omitted from the survival list. 6.6 / 7.5

Contradiction in liability provisions: 7.3 carves Security Incidents caused by Provider negligence out of the cap, while 7.4 states the cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of the Agreement. 7.3 / 7.4
Governing law versus jurisdiction contradiction: 8.3 selects Washington law while 8.4 requires Delaware courts to apply Delaware law to any dispute. 8.3 / 8.4
Fee contradiction with the Service Catalog: Appendix A's line items total $4,690 per month, but Section 3.2 states the monthly Fee is $4,750 — a $60 discrepancy. Appendix A / 3.2
Inconsistent support metric: Appendix A item A-3 promises a '4 hour response' whereas 5.2 promises four 'Business Hours', which are different (and undefined) measures. Appendix A A-3 / 5.2
Logical gap: 'Confidential Information' is defined but no section imposes any confidentiality obligation, so the definition is orphaned. 1.3 (no operative confidentiality section)

Potential conflict: 2.2 permits Provider to modify performance unilaterally, while 2.4 requires any change to the scope of Services to follow a written change control procedure; the boundary between the two is unspecified. 2.2 / 2.4

Conflict between remedies: 5.6 makes service credits the sole remedy for service level failures, which conflicts with 7.3's uncapped liability route for negligence-caused Security Incidents affecting availability, and with 5.5's cap leaving unremedied loss. 5.6 / 7.3

Definition of 'Security Incident' covers only unauthorized access or disclosure, omitting loss, destruction, alteration or unavailability of Personal Data, leaving the notification duty in 4.5/4.7 incomplete. 1.6
Appendix A item A-5 is listed as 'Reserved' with no description or charge, leaving an undefined placeholder in the contractual service catalog. Appendix A A-5

Section 3.7 permits 1.5% monthly interest (approx. 19.6% per annum compounded) without any cap or savings clause tied to the applicable usury law, and no cross-reference to the governing law provisions that themselves conflict. 3.7

Undefined term "Business Hours" used for the Priority 1 response time (distinct from the defined "Business Day"). 5.2
"Permitted Subprocessor" is defined but never used in the operative text; Section 4.8 addresses subprocessors without using the defined term, making the definition orphaned. 1.7 / 4.8
"Effective Date" is used in the preamble and Sections 2 and 6 but never defined in Section 1; it is defined only by reference to a superseded agreement. 1 / 6.1
Arithmetic error: twelve monthly payments of $4,750 equal $57,000, not the stated annual fee of $58,000. 3.3 (with 3.2)
Direct contradiction: Section 3.5 gives a 45-day term for invoices over $10,000 while Section 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception". 3.5 / 3.6
Fee inconsistency: the monthly Fee stated as $4,750 conflicts with Appendix A's total monthly charge of $4,690 (a $60 discrepancy). 3.2 / Appendix A
Direct contradiction in Security Incident notification deadline: 72 hours in 4.5 versus three (3) Business Days in 4.7 (which can be substantially longer over weekends/holidays). 4.5 / 4.7
Arithmetic error: 99.5% monthly availability permits roughly 3.6 hours of downtime in a 30-day month (0.5% of 720–744 hours), not the stated three (3) hours. 5.3
Contradiction: the 25% (and the combined 10%) service credit tiers in 5.4 exceed the aggregate cap of 10% of the monthly Fee in 5.5, so the stated remedy can never be paid. 5.4 / 5.5
Overlapping/ambiguous credit tiers: availability below 95% is simultaneously below 99% and below 99.5%, so multiple tiers apply with no rule of precedence or non-cumulation. 5.4

Logical gap: Section 5.1 imposes only a "commercially reasonable efforts" standard, yet 5.4 imposes automatic credits for failure to achieve fixed levels — the obligation standard and the remedy trigger are inconsistent. 5.1 / 5.4

Circular/contradictory Effective Date: 6.1 defines it by reference to the prior Master Services Agreement, which 8.1 says this Agreement supersedes, and 8.1 separately fixes effectiveness at 1 January 2027. 6.1 / 8.1
Internal contradiction in termination for breach: termination is stated to be "immediately on written notice" yet conditioned on a 15-day uncured cure period. 6.4

Contradiction: 6.5 prohibits shortening or waiving the 60-day notice period, which conflicts with the immediate termination right in 6.4 and with the parties' ability to agree otherwise. 6.3 / 6.4 / 6.5
Survival inconsistency: 6.6 lists only Sections 1, 4 and 8 as surviving, while 7.5 states Section 7 survives termination. 6.6 / 7.5
Contradiction: 7.4 states the liability cap applies "notwithstanding any other provision", which nullifies the express carve-out in 7.3 for negligent Security Incidents. 7.3 / 7.4

Logical gap in the mutual cap: liability of "each party" is capped by reference to Fees paid by Customer, giving no measurable cap where Customer has prepaid nothing or where Provider claims against Customer in the first months. 7.2
Conflict of governing law/forum: 8.3 selects Washington law while 8.4 confers exclusive jurisdiction on Delaware courts applying Delaware law. 8.3 / 8.4

Conflict between 2.2 (Provider may unilaterally modify performance) and 2.4 (any change to scope requires written agreement under change control), with no boundary between "manner of performance" and "scope". 2.2 / 2.4
Appendix A item A-3 promises a "4 hour response" whereas 5.2 promises four Business Hours — inconsistent measurement of the same commitment. Appendix A / 5.2
Appendix A charges a quarterly deliverable (A-4 Quarterly analytics review) as a monthly charge without stating how the quarterly service maps to monthly billing. Appendix A
Sole remedy clause in 5.6 conflicts with the uncapped liability carve-out and general liability regime in Section 7 (e.g., a Security Incident causing downtime), with no reconciliation. 5.6 / 7.3
Definition of Security Incident omits loss, destruction, or alteration of Personal Data, so 4.5/4.7 notification duties do not cover common breach types. 1.6
Section 8.1 states the Agreement "takes effect on 1 January 2027" while the preamble says it takes effect on the Effective Date — two different effectiveness triggers. Preamble / 8.1

findings: "Confidential Information" is defined circularly — "information that is confidential" — providing no operative test for what qualifies 1.3

Arithmetic error/contradiction: monthly Fee of $4,750 × 12 = $57,000, not the $58,000 stated as "twelve monthly payments" 3.3
Monthly Fee of $4,750 contradicts Appendix A's total monthly charge of $4,690 (a $60 discrepancy) 3.2
Direct contradiction: 3.5 gives 45-day terms for invoices over $10,000, but 3.6 states the 30-day term applies to all invoices "without exception" 3.5 / 3.6
"Restricted Data" is an undefined term; the Agreement elsewhere uses the defined term "Personal Data" 4.2

Tension between the "commercially reasonable efforts" standard in 5.1 and the strict, measured availability commitment with automatic credits in 5.3–5.4 5.1

Liability cap measured by "Fees paid by Customer" is applied to both parties, leaving Customer's own liability capped by its own payments — an incoherent mutual cap 7.2
